fortifier_type: N/A

population_detail: VLBW infants 2010-2022, stratified by antenatal Doppler pattern (normal; UA-AREDF alone; UA+DV-AREDF; brain-sparing redistribution)

fortifier_type: not addressed

n_patients: 25 AREDF pregnancies (19 morphologically normal fetuses) vs matched controls

fortifier_type: N/A

population_detail: pregnancies with hypertension and/or IUGR, Doppler-studied

fortifier_type: N/A

design: Systematic review (19 studies: 2 case series, 1 cohort, 16 historical-control)
n_patients: varies by included study, not pooled

outcomes_measured: time to first feed; incidence of SIP; time to full enteral feeds; PN duration; LOS; neurodevelopmental outcome; mortality (primary: time to first feed)

design: Prospective cohort vs historic comparison group

outcomes_measured: time to restart feeds; time to full enteral feeds; central-line duration; catheter sepsis; LOS; NEC recurrence/death
primary_result: Early feeding associated with shorter time to full feeds, shorter central-line duration, less catheter sepsis, shorter LOS, with no apparent increase in NEC recurrence or death
effect_size: Feeds restarted median 4d (range 3-14) vs 10d (range 8-22); full feeds 10d (range7-31) vs 19d (range9-76); LOS 63d vs 69d

secondary_results: 1 NEC-related death in early group vs 2 in comparison group; 2 vs 1 recurrent NEC
ascertainment_method: prospective protocol-driven cohort vs historic controls
rob_domains: historic (non-concurrent) control group — confounded by secular changes in NICU care
rob_overall: high risk of bias (non-randomised, historic control)
directness: Direct for sub-question (i) [restarting ANY feeding after NEC] but says nothing about fortifier timing specifically (sub-question ii)
grade_reason: Non-randomised historic-control design; explicitly underpowered (as authors themselves state) to exclude a higher NEC-recurrence risk
key_limitation: Authors themselves state the study was underpowered to exclude increased recurrence risk — an important self-acknowledged limitation to preserve in synthesis
notes: Landmark early-refeeding-after-NEC cohort named in the brief; says nothing about fortifier re-introduction specifically
fortifier_type: not addressed

population_detail: premature neonates with surgical NEC

rob_overall: (very) low certainty for most recommendations, per the guideline panel's own assessment

grade_certainty: Very low (per guideline's own GRADE label on most recommendations)

design: Joint position paper (expert consensus, literature review 1990-Sept2024)

outcomes_measured: expert suggestions, not graded pooled effect estimates

effect_size: N/A (expert consensus, not evidence synthesis with effect sizes)

grade_reason: Explicitly expert-opinion / consensus-based due to absence of RCTs in this field, as stated by the authors themselves
key_limitation: Second independent confirmation (alongside ERNICA 2024) that no fortifier-specific guidance exists for post-surgical NEC/SIP refeeding — the evidence gap is corroborated across two independent guideline/position-paper efforts

fortifier_type: not addressed

design: Cochrane systematic review and meta-analysis (18 RCTs)
population_detail: preterm infants fed human milk
outcomes_measured: in-hospital weight gain, length, head circumference velocity; NEC; other morbidity/mortality; long-term growth/ND (limited data)
primary_result: Fortification increases in-hospital weight, length and head-circumference growth velocity; low-certainty evidence of NO clear effect on NEC risk
effect_size: Weight MD 1.76 g/kg/d; Length MD 0.11 cm/wk; HC MD 0.06 cm/wk; NEC RR 1.37
secondary_results: Data on growth/ND beyond infancy sparse and show no clear fortification effect; evidence insufficient to determine long-term impact
ascertainment_method: Cochrane Neonatal standard methods, 2 authors independent extraction, GRADE
rob_domains: trials generally small and methodologically weak
rob_overall: Low to moderate certainty overall (per Cochrane's own GRADE, not re-derived)
directness: Direct (preterm, human milk fed)
grade_certainty: Low-Moderate (varies by outcome; growth = low-moderate, NEC = low)
grade_reason: Small trials, methodological weakness (per Cochrane authors' own assessment) = risk of bias domain
key_limitation: THE core Domain-4 evidence base; growth benefit is real but modest and long-term/ND data essentially absent — must not be over-interpreted as a growth-to-outcome causal chain
notes: Current (2020) update of the review the brief cites as 'Brown 2016' (PMID 27155888, CD000343.pub3, now superseded) — this synthesis uses the current version's numbers, noting the brief's citation year is one version behind
fortifier_type: multi-nutrient (mixed/not product-specific)

design: Systematic review and meta-analysis (15 RCTs), RoB2 + INSPECT-SR trustworthiness tool
population_detail: neonates <=34 weeks GA or <=2500g birthweight
outcomes_measured: weight/length/HC gain velocity; feeding intolerance; NEC; late-onset sepsis; CLD; time to full enteral feeds; LOS; mortality

p_value: significant for growth; NS for morbidity outcomes
secondary_results: Substantial heterogeneity (I2 87-95%) for growth outcomes; INSPECT-SR flagged 1 trial with serious trustworthiness concerns, 12 with some concerns, 2 with none
ascertainment_method: PRISMA, RoB2, random-effects models, INSPECT-SR trustworthiness screening (novel addition)
rob_domains: substantial heterogeneity; trustworthiness concerns in most included trials
rob_overall: Low certainty overall (per authors)
directness: Direct (preterm/LBW)
grade_reason: Substantial unexplained heterogeneity (imprecision/inconsistency) and trial-trustworthiness concerns per authors' own INSPECT-SR screening
key_limitation: This is the brief's anticipated '2026 update' to Brown et al. — larger effect estimates than the Cochrane review but explicitly flagged by its own authors as low-certainty due to heterogeneity and trustworthiness concerns; do not treat as superseding Cochrane's more conservative estimate without noting this caveat
notes: Uses novel INSPECT-SR tool for study trustworthiness — a methodological strength worth naming explicitly in synthesis
fortifier_type: not specified/mixed

population_detail: preterm neonates, various feeding regimens including multi-nutrient fortification
outcomes_measured: mortality, NEC, ROP, sepsis, PVL, BPD, time to full enteral feeds, Bayley II MDI
primary_result: Mother's own milk + donor milk + human-milk-based fortifier ranked top for mortality, NEC and time to full feeds; mother's own milk + phosphorus fortifier ranked top for ROP/BPD; insufficient high-quality evidence to support/refute any single regimen definitively
effect_size: treatment rankings (SUCRA-style), not single pooled effect sizes in abstract
secondary_results: Sex-based/product-based ranking varied substantially by outcome, underscoring inconsistency across the evidence network
ascertainment_method: Cochrane CENTRAL/Medline/Embase/CINAHL to June 2023, 2 independent reviewers
rob_domains: network meta-analysis assumptions (transitivity) not detailed in abstract
rob_overall: Low (per authors' own conclusion of 'insufficient high-quality evidence')
directness: Direct (preterm)
grade_reason: Authors' own conclusion states insufficient high-quality evidence to support or refute any regimen — network inconsistency and indirect comparisons downgrade certainty
key_limitation: Useful for showing DIRECTION of ranked preference (HM-derived fortifier tends to rank favourably) but explicitly not strong enough evidence to mandate practice change
notes: First global network-meta-analytic view of fortification/feeding-regimen combinations per the authors' own framing
fortifier_type: multiple (network compares regimen classes)
bmf_terminology_check: Does not use BMF; uses 'bovine fortifier' as one network node

design: Follow-up study of RCT (6-year corrected age)
n_patients: 214 (141 breastfed [randomised F-MOM vs U-MOM] + 73 preterm-formula group)
population_detail: very preterm infants, followed to 6 years corrected age
intervention: Post-discharge fortification of mother's own milk (F-MOM)
comparator: Unfortified mother's own milk (U-MOM); separately, preterm formula (PF) group
outcomes_measured: Full-scale IQ (WISC-IV); subdomain scores; Five to Fifteen (FTF) parent questionnaire domains
primary_result: Post-discharge fortification of MOM did NOT improve full-scale IQ or any FTF domain score vs unfortified MOM (essentially null)
effect_size: Median FSIQ 104 (F-MOM) vs 105.5 (U-MOM)
secondary_results: MOM group (fortified or not) had significantly better verbal comprehension (110 vs 106, P=0.03) and motor FTF scores (P=0.01) than the preterm-formula group
ascertainment_method: WISC-IV cognitive testing + FTF parent questionnaire at 6yr CA
rob_tool: not specified (RCT follow-up, but attrition not detailed in abstract)
rob_domains: follow-up attrition not quantified in abstract
rob_overall: moderate (long-interval follow-up, attrition risk)
directness: DIRECT and Tier (i) per brief's directness taxonomy — fortification was the randomised variable and the outcome is a formal, hard neurodevelopmental endpoint (IQ), not a surrogate
grade_reason: Single RCT follow-up with a clinically important, well-validated hard outcome (IQ) but some downgrade for unspecified attrition and single-centre/country generalisability
key_limitation: THE key Domain-5 Tier-i null finding — post-discharge fortification does not move the needle on IQ at school age; must be given full prominence per the brief's null-finding rule, not buried under positive surrogate-outcome findings elsewhere
notes: Cross-referenced in Domain 7 (post-discharge) — same trial, two relevant domains
fortifier_type: bovine (implied, standard HMF for post-discharge fortification) — not explicitly BMF-labelled
fortification_definition: post-discharge, shortly before discharge to 4 months corrected age

outcomes_measured: Bayley-III cognitive, language, motor composite scores at 18 months corrected age; death or neurodevelopmental impairment/disability

effect_size: Cognitive: 94.7 (HMBF) vs 95.9 (BMBF), MD -1.1
p_value: NS for all three composite domains
secondary_results: No difference in proportion with death or neurodevelopmental impairment/disability between groups

key_limitation: Directly answers 'does fortifier SOURCE (human vs bovine) affect neurodevelopment' — answer is no, at 18 months; this is a different question from Klamer 2022's 'does fortifying at all vs not' question
notes: Follow-up of the O'Connor 2018 AJCN RCT (D8- entry below); BMBF here explicitly = bovine milk-based fortifier, the brief's reserved 'BMF' sense
fortifier_type: human-milk-derived vs bovine-derived (explicit HMBF vs BMBF comparison)

population_detail: preterm infants <30 weeks gestation
outcomes_measured: weight gain, growth velocity, body composition at 36wk PMA; Bayley-III at 18 months CA
primary_result: TFO significantly increased weight gain and growth velocity; Bayley-III scores numerically higher across cognitive/language/motor domains in TFO group, mostly not reaching statistical significance except expressive language in a subgroup
effect_size: Weight gain 2514+/-289g (TFO) vs 2283+/-332g (SF), P<0.01; growth velocity 21.7+/-2.3 vs 19.2+/-2.2 g/kg/d, P<0.001
